teams.heading: Mick Byrne departed Fiji head coach role in April by mutual agreement
teams.body: Fiji continue to seek a permanent head coach following Mick Byrne's departure by mutual agreement in April. The Australian, who was appointed in 2024, stepped down to allow Fiji Rugby to pursue a new direction, stating it had been 'an honour to work with the Flying Fijians players and staff'. CEO Koli Sewabu confirmed the exit ahead of the July Nations Championship, leaving the post vacant as Fiji prepare to face France.

teams.heading: Joe Carpenter targets George Furbank duel to reignite England ambitions
teams.body: Sale full-back Joe Carpenter is using this weekend’s clash against Harlequins as a direct audition to challenge George Furbank for the England jersey. Carpenter, who has not featured for Steve Borthwick since July 2025, has benefited from a full pre-season and is currently among the Premiership’s most prolific defenders beaten. Regarding his motivation for the head-to-head, Carpenter said, "Yeah I'd say so, in a certain aspect," noting that outshining his direct rival is key to forcing his way into the squad for November.

teams.heading: Victor Wembanyama trains with French rugby club to develop physical strength
teams.body: NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama recently spent part of his off-season training with Provence Rugby. The 22-year-old sought to improve his game through the physical and mental rigours of rugby, participating in line-out drills, tackling sessions and passing practice alongside the second-tier side. Wembanyama praised the camaraderie of the squad, noting that he was inspired by the unity he witnessed. The basketball star previously worked on stability and movement patterns during his visit to the French club in August.

teams.heading: Aoife Wafer ruled out of Ireland women’s squad for South Africa
teams.body: The Ireland women’s team will travel to South Africa for their upcoming WXV Global Series fixtures without star back-rower Aoife Wafer. The 23-year-old Harlequins player, who missed the recent consecutive victories against Japan due to a minor training injury, has failed to recover in time for the two-match tour. Scott Bemand’s 30-player squad, captained by Erin King, will head to Cape Town later this month as they look to build on their current momentum.

teams.heading: Scottish Rugby and Macron launch new vintage-inspired 'Archive Collection' range
teams.body: Scottish Rugby has partnered with Macron to release 'The Archive Collection', a range reimagining fan-favourite kits from the 1990s and early 2000s. Filmed at the historic Inverleith Sports Ground, the campaign features current internationals such as Ewan Ashman and Pierre Schoeman alongside legends including Chris Paterson and Jason White. Head of retail David Salisbury stated, “We decided this was the right time to bring back and reimagine some of these favourites,” noting the goal is to connect historic visual identities with modern relevance.

lead.why: The launch of The Archive Collection is a fresh development reported by the national union today.

teams.heading: WRU publishes Keystone report data justifying future professional team cuts
teams.body: The Welsh Rugby Union has released the independent Keystone report, the 68-page document central to the governing body’s plan to reduce the number of professional men’s sides from four to three by 2028. The data outlines the methodology behind the board’s decision to prioritise licences for Cardiff and Dragons in the east. This follows sustained criticism from fans and stakeholders in west Wales, where Ospreys and Scarlets remain locked in an ongoing struggle to retain their professional status.

lead.why: The publication of the Keystone report data provides formal justification for the controversial regional restructuring plan that remains the primary institutional story in Welsh rugby.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards joins Argentina as defence coach until 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi has confirmed the appointment of Shaun Edwards as Argentina’s new defence coach, a move that secures the former France assistant’s services until the 2027 World Cup in Australia. Edwards, who will begin his role at the end of October alongside returning forwards coach Mario Ledesma, expressed his excitement to bring international experience to the squad. Contepomi noted that both men arrive with immense experience and understand what is required to compete at the highest level of the game.

teams.heading: Les Kiss persists with Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on wing for Bledisloe Test
teams.body: Wallabies coach Les Kiss has opted for continuity by keeping Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on the wing for the Bledisloe Cup opener at Eden Park. The decision follows a successful shift from the midfield during the recent victory over the Springboks in Perth. Kiss emphasised the importance of maintaining the back-three combination, noting that the aerial game will be vital against the All Blacks. The coach remains optimistic about the impact of Suaalii’s physicality in a venue where Australia has not tasted victory since 1986.

teams.heading: Japan Sakura Sevens Reclaim Asian Games Gold In Nagoya Victory
teams.body: Japan’s women secured gold at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, defeating defending champions China 10-5 in a tightly contested final. The Sakura Sevens successfully reclaimed the title they last held two Games ago. While the host nation’s men were defeated in the semifinal by China, they recovered to claim bronze by beating Korea 17-5. The victory for the women highlights a dominant performance across the tournament, reinforcing their position within the continental rugby sevens landscape.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie wields the axe as All Blacks face Bledisloe pressure
teams.body: Head coach Dave Rennie has made 11 personnel changes for the Bledisloe Cup opener, including the omission of tighthead prop Tyrel Lomax. Former All Black James Parsons noted that Rennie’s willingness to drop established players creates a necessary "edge" in the camp to drive accountability. Facing a crucial test after recent defeats, Rennie admitted the squad has openly discussed the pressure of defending their long-standing unbeaten record at Eden Park, choosing to embrace that history as "fuel" for the upcoming challenge.

teams.heading: Eddie O’Sullivan highlights Springboks’ ‘frightening’ scrum as major Ireland concern
teams.body: Former Ireland boss Eddie O’Sullivan has warned that South Africa’s set-piece dominance poses a significant tactical problem for Andy Farrell’s side ahead of their meeting next month. Citing recent URC set-piece struggles as evidence, O’Sullivan noted that the current Springbok power game is dominating international rugby. He described the South African scrum as “frightening to watch,” and suggested that the physicality of the world champions remains a challenge that other international teams are currently struggling to contain as they head into the November tests.

lead.why: It addresses a specific technical concern regarding the Springboks' dominance that is already creating debate ahead of the upcoming international window.
